signals.name: EUR/USD
signals.label: Volatility squeeze breakout
signals.exit_txt: Stop 1.5 ATR, target 3 ATR, time-stop 15 sessions.
signals.why: Volatility clusters and mean-reverts (Engle ARCH 1982); compressed ranges tend to be followed by range expansion, so a breakout from a squeeze has a better payoff profile.
reasons: Bollinger width in the bottom 15% of the last year within the past 5 sessions (now 52th pct)
Close 1.1025 below prior 20-day low 1.1027
History on EUR/USD: 35 trades, hit 46% (95% CI 30-62%), avg +0.17R net of costs
Out-of-sample (last 30% of trades): +0.55R per trade
In the current normal-volatility regime: 14 trades, avg -0.27R
Data caveat: Large open-vs-previous-close gaps (median 0.45x avg range): feed mixes sessions or futures rolls -> backtest fills are less reliable
signals.invalidation: Thesis is wrong if price trades above 1.1138 (=-1R) or nothing happens by 2026-12-07.

signals.name: S&P 500
signals.label: Trend pullback (RSI-2)
signals.entry_txt: Next session open (or limit 0.25 ATR better).
signals.exit_txt: Stop 1.5 ATR, target 1.5 ATR, time-stop 7 sessions.
signals.why: Short-term mean reversion inside a long-term trend (Connors RSI-2; short-horizon reversal documented by Jegadeesh 1990 / Lehmann 1990). You buy fear inside an up-trend.
reasons: Price above 200-day average (7,416.59 vs 7,342.71) -> long-term trend is up
12-month momentum +10.1% confirms the trend
RSI(2) = 9.8 -> short-term oversold (trigger <10)
